title: Cæsar Frederiks agtien-jarige reys, na en door Indien, anno 1563 en vervolgens, seer naauwkeurig door hem selfs beschreven. ; Nu aldereerst uyt het Engelsch vertaald. Met nodige konstprinten, en een volkomen register verrĳkt
shelf_note: No tradition or collection set; the leaf is a 1706 Dutch Fraktur printing of Federici's travels, consistent with the record (title, author, date, language).
structure_note: structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book's pages_translated field says 80 (and this page has a translation), so the counts disagree. 4 backsteps and 5 repeats among 63 printed numbers in a 94-record book probably come from unnumbered plates (the title promises 'konstprinten') or misread numerals, not a splice. This page is consistent: running head '19', signature 'B 2'.

pages.layout: single column of Fraktur with roman for names, running head with page number, two marginal notes in the outer (right) margin, signature and catchword at the foot

ocr_errors.problem: Fraktur F misread as K, so 'fustas' (galleys) becomes 'coasts'

ocr_errors.ocr: Ik kwam in mijn reyse by getal ter plaats
ocr_errors.image: Ik quam in mijn reys by geval ter plaats
ocr_errors.problem: 'geval' (chance) misread as 'getal' (number), and 'quam'/'reys' normalised to 'kwam'/'reyse'; the translation follows the image ('by chance')

tr_errors.english: <note>The print reads "Kusten", most likely a misprint for "Fusten".</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note blames the print for an OCR misreading: the image clearly reads 'Fusten', so there is no misprint. This is false apparatus about the source, even though the rendering 'fustas' is correct
the source's own gloss 'of wagtplaats' (or guard post) is dropped from the body and appears only inside the editorial gloss

other.note: invented apparatus: a note asserts that 'The print reads "Kusten"', which the image beside it shows is false (it reads 'Fusten')

book_verdict: The transcription and translation of this Fraktur page are good. One Fraktur misread ('Kusten' for 'Fusten') is corrected in the English, but a note then blames the print for the misprint, which is false scholarship an expert would catch against the image. The book's translated-page counts disagree.
